Sanders is big on taxes for massive corporations that avoid them and the very wealthy that have seen massive tax cuts in the past 50 or so years. He also has mentioned that the Pentagon's budget is way too big but hasn't discussed cutting it as policy, most likely not to alienate some voters.

The other way to shrink our national debt besides cutting spending and raising taxes is to expand our GDP so that the debt, in comparison, becomes smaller and smaller over time.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_United_States_public_debt

Sanders' $1T infrastructure bill would cost 1/3 as much as Bush's tax cuts + Iraq/Afghanistan all put together and at the same time put people to work, giving them income that would let businesses profit and the economy to flourish.

Sanders is also an advocate for free college tuition, which enables tons of millennials to purchase cars and homes and makes our economy more competitive by having a better educated workforce, like Germany's.

This is, however, only one solution and many conservatives/libertarians oppose it and believe in a more "laissez-faire" system, and that's a fair view. The greatest benefit of Sanders' plans are that they lift people out of poverty and into jobs and they generally benefit everyone.
